workAndWages.title: Work and wages
workAndWages.standfirst: A law gave every rural household the right to 100 days of paid work, and from February 2006 the first districts began to offer it.

items.title: What the Act promised
items.summary: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act passed the Lok Sabha on 23 August and the Rajya Sabha on 25 August 2005, received assent on 5 September, and began on 2 February 2006, promising at least 100 days of paid unskilled work a year to rural households that volunteer for it.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005
Wikipedia: 2005 in India

items.title: An allowance if no work comes
items.summary: Applicants are entitled to an unemployment allowance if work is not provided within 15 days of applying.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005

items.title: How far it reached
items.summary: The programme began in a pilot of 625 districts and covered all districts from 1 April 2008, on average giving work to about 5 crore (50 million) households a year since then; 12 crore (120 million) job cards had been issued by 2012, and wages ranged from Rs 122 in Bihar and Jharkhand to Rs 191 in Haryana.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005

keepingInTouch.title: Keeping in touch
keepingInTouch.standfirst: Phone calls abroad got cheaper, and when the rains came to Mumbai millions lost their connection.

items.title: Cheaper bandwidth
items.summary: On 10 March 2005 TRAI cut international bandwidth tariffs by up to 70 percent, effective 1 April.

healthAndMedicine.title: Health and medicine
healthAndMedicine.standfirst: A commission ruled that hospitals must treat emergencies before asking for money.

items.title: Treat first
items.summary: On 25 April 2005 the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission ruled that hospitals must accept accident victims and critically ill patients, that doctors cannot demand fees before treating, and that relatives' consent is not needed when no family member is present.

sources.label: Wikipedia: 2005 in India

leisureAndFun.title: Evenings, weekends and festivals
leisureAndFun.standfirst: The multiplex had been in India since 1997, and in 2005 a leading chain was opening one in a mall every few months.

items.title: The first multiplex
items.summary: PVR's company history says it opened India's first multiplex cinema, PVR Anupam in Saket, New Delhi, in June 1997 and by 2003 to 2005 was adding screens in malls in Gurgaon, Bangalore, Faridabad and East Delhi (March 2005).

items.title: Fifty-one screens
items.summary: With 51 screens as of February 2006, PVR was the largest multiplex operator in India.

spotlight.title: The mobile phone and SMS boom
spotlight.standfirst: Mobile phones went from rarity to a necessity for urban India within the decade, as calls became cheaper and networks multiplied.

items.title: From 0.3 to 7.8 per hundred
items.summary: Mobile subscriptions rose from 0.34 per 100 people in 2000 to 7.8 in 2005 and 60.5 in 2010.

sources.label: World Bank, World Development Indicators: Mobile cellular subscriptions (per 100 people)

items.title: New operators
items.summary: Reliance Communications began operating in 2004, and Escotel, which started in 1996, ceased in 2004 and was merged into Idea Cellular.
